title: Audit harness + retroactive crediting flow for speculative prefetches in multipart streaming
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We have increasing customer reports and internal audit traces showing sporadic overcharges caused by server-side speculative prefetching of future stream fragments. The runtime prefetches next-sequence fragments to reduce tail latency; when clients abort, reconnect, or the server falls back to a cheaper model, provisional credits for prefetched fragments are sometimes never reclaimed and become permanent charges. This ticket adds an audit harness to exercise speculative prefetch paths and implements a retroactive crediting flow to safely refund unused prefetched tokens without violating idempotency or opening race conditions with concurrent commits.
acceptance_criteria: Audit harness can simulate 8 prefetch scenarios (normal completion, client abort, reconnect with partial replay, midstream model switch, speculative decode failure, server-side fallback, backpressure-caused drop, duplicate fragment arrival) and emit deterministic trace vectors

Retroactive crediting flow correctly issues negative adjustments for unused prefetched fragments in 99.999% of synthetic runs (measured by harness) with zero false-negatives where a legitimately consumed token is refunded
Credits are applied idempotently (replaying the same reconciliation job does not double-refund), verified by unit tests and a 48-hour shadow run against production ledger copies
No regressions in normal path latency (<2ms p50 increase) and no visible increase in upstream error rates
Documentation and runbook for investigating refunds and a dashboard showing refunded volume by customer and by scenario
technical_notes: Design summary: introduce 'provisional' ledger records for prefetch allocations with fields: fragment_uuid, session_uuid, provisional=true, origin_hint, prefetch_window_id. When a fragment is actually consumed, we atomically flip provisional->committed (commit record with same fragment_uuid). For cleanup, a reconciliation worker scans provisional records older than watermark + jitter and applies a reconciliation strategy: 1) if commit exists: no-op; 2) if commit absent and session terminated/aborted: emit a single idempotent refund record referencing original provisional entry; 3) if commit absent and session resumed with conflicting fragment_uuid (duplicate detection): run merge logic to attribute consumption to the earliest provisional and refund later duplicates. Implementation details: use event-sourced append-only ledger, deterministic reconciliation job with monotonic watermark per-session, per-model-version, and fragment_uuid-based idempotency token. We will also add a compacted index for provisional->commit lookup to keep worker latency low. Trade-offs: maintaining provisional records increases storage and index overhead (~3-5% token ledger increase) but avoids heavy synchronous checks that would harm tail latency.
test_plan: Unit tests: provisional lifecycle (create->commit->refund->replay); idempotency tests for duplicate refund attempts; merge scenarios for fragmented duplicates. Integration: harness runs 10k synthetic sessions across prefetch scenarios with deterministic seeds and verifies final ledger invariants (total_charged = baseline_consumed + net_provisional_committed - net_refunded). Shadow run: run reconciliation job in audit-only mode against a production copy for 14 days; collect diffs and verify no customer-facing refunds will be emitted without manual review. Chaos tests: simulate worker restarts, out-of-order events, and clock skew to validate watermark correctness.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged deployment of provisional ledger schema and reconciliation worker in shadow/audit mode (no refunds) for 2 weeks. 2) After validation, enable refunds for internal customers only for 48 hours. 3) Gradually open refunds to low-volume customers and monitor refund-to-charge ratios and dispute volume for 7 days. 4) If metrics are within thresholds, full rollout. Metrics and thresholds: refund_rate<0.5% of total tokens, disputes per 1M tokens < 3, p99 reconciliation job latency < 5s. Rollback path: disable refund emitter and pause reconciliation worker; report platform metrics and run manual investigation.
